newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian party blames Howard for rise of Hanson.
newsitem.headline: Australian party blames Howard for rise of Hanson.

text.p: An Australian minority party on Monday blamed Prime Minister John Howard for the political momentum of MP Pauline Hanson, a controverserial independent who has campaigned against Asian immigration and Aboriginal welfare.
Australian Democrats Leader Cheryl Kernot said Howard should have taken a stand against Hanson sooner, rather than repeatedly dodging the issue by saying she was entitled to her own views.
"After hearing that a hundred times, it seemed to me he shouldn't wonder that the momentum was able to be built up," Kernot told reporters.
"He should not wonder at the damage that was able to be done (to Australia's standing) in Asia."
The Liberal-National government launched a political offensive against Hanson last week after an opinion poll showed her with 10 percent voter support.
In her first first parliamentary speech last September Hanson claimed, among other things, that Australian was in danger of being swamped by Asians.
This provoked a storm of protest and, distressingly for the main political parties, much voter support for Hanson.
Howard and his government barely responded, even though the row was well-publicised in Asia.
But since last week's opinion poll a succession of senior ministers have taken potshots at her.
Treasurer Peter Costello, who normally sticks to economics, said on Sunday that Hanson was promulgating a divisive and vicious future for the country.
Hanson also attracted rowdy protesters to a speech she made in Perth on Sunday and on Monday she complained that the major political parties were inciting verbal attacks on her.
"I live through each day with increasing threats against myself and my family and all of this with the encouragement, indeed barracking, of Liberal and Labor politicians," Hanson said in a statement.
Labor opposition leader Kim Beazley showed no sympathy. "Expect the torpedoes," he advised Hanson.
